In the following appendix , we derive the entropy of adsorption in the case of infinite dilution and show how it may be related to familiar thermodynamic quantities ( cf . eq 5 ) . To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as $$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$ where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. Although these simulations are numerically cleaner compared to experiment because they involve analyzing efficiently a greater number of molecule–zeolite combinations, it remains overwhelming to apply them to the millions of hypothetical frameworks. descriptor_candidate.rationale: SPAN is a heavy-atom (implicit-H) enclosing radius about the center of mass and serves as a crude adsorbate rotational-extent proxy; its legitimate zeros (single-atom/single-site species) give a descriptor value of 0, meaning 'no resolved rotational confinement proxy', which is preserved rather than imputed. lsd_p is Zeo++ Dif, the largest included sphere along the free-sphere path; it is NOT the global cavity diameter Di and NOT the passing bottleneck Df, so the mapping from the source 'average cavity diameter' narrative onto lsd_p is an explicit approximation: it characterizes the space available along the diffusion path rather than a specific cage. The mechanism assumed (rotation-family) is that tighter inclusion along the path restricts rotational degrees of freedom more, consistent with the reported greater rotational entropy loss in smaller-pore zeolites. The ratio is dimensionless by construction (q-ratio); no literal threshold of 1 is assumed to be a physical equality.
descriptor_candidate.falsification_criteria: The descriptor is falsified as a rotational-confinement proxy if: (1) within the training support, entropy loss over R systematically decreases (or is flat) as q_SPAN/q_lsd_p increases at fixed framework geometry, indicating translational/configurational or chemistry terms dominate instead; (2) cage-type and channel-type frameworks with identical descriptor values show systematically different losses, indicating lsd_p along the free path fails to represent the confinement space relevant to rotation (competing explanation: global cavity Di or accessible volume governs the loss); (3) the relation holds only for linear alkanes and breaks for the nonlinear majority of the training adsorbates.
proxy_assumptions: SPAN (implicit-H heavy-atom enclosing radius) is assumed to correlate with the adsorbate's rotational spatial extent; hydrogens and exact all-atom geometry are not represented.

This is a falsifiable proxy hypothesis transferring the reported MFI/FAU and FER/FAU confinement-rotation comparisons to this benchmark's infinite-dilution entropy-loss target; it is not an established law.
final_candidate.rationale: Mechanism: geometric confinement restricts adsorbate rotational and configurational freedom, which the cited zeolite comparisons associate with larger entropy loss in smaller-pore frameworks. The ratio GeDi/lsd_f expresses molecule span relative to the bottleneck as a dimensionless confinement proxy. Proxy limitations: lsd_f (Zeo++ Df) is the largest sphere able to pass through a periodic free path, NOT the global cavity diameter Di that the source comparisons reference, so the mapping from 'cavity diameter' to Df is an explicit approximation; GeDi is a heavy-atom pair distance in the implicit-H representation, not a van der Waals contact span, and it is legitimately zero for 54 single-site training cases (ratio then 0, not excluded); lsd_f has no zeros in training (min 0.85684 A) so the ratio is finite across training support. final_candidate.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if, within the training regime (lsd_f in [0.85684, 7.68726] A, GeDi in [0, 10.97181443] A), entropy_loss_over_R does not decrease with increasing lsd_f at fixed GeDi, or if the apparent relation disappears when ASA/AV (probe-accessible area/volume) are held fixed — indicating the signal is explained by overall framework accessibility rather than bottleneck confinement. final_candidate.proxy_assumptions: Assumes (1) the bottleneck free-sphere diameter Df is an adequate stand-in for the cavity-diameter confinement measure used in the reported FER/FAU comparison, even though Df, Dif, and global Di are distinct quantities; (2) the largest heavy-atom pair distance GeDi proxies the molecular rotational envelope, ignoring hydrogens and side-group orientations; (3) infinite-dilution, rigid-framework conditions comparable to the target; (4) rotational confinement dominates the entropy-loss variation attributable to this descriptor, with translational contributions left to other descriptors. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. draft.name: bottleneck_pair_span_ratio
draft.hypothesis: Conditional on the same adsorbate (GeDi held fixed), frameworks with a larger largest free passing sphere (lsd_f) allow more retained rotational and configurational freedom, so the reported pattern that stronger geometric confinement coincides with larger entropy loss on adsorption implies entropy_loss_over_R decreases as lsd_f increases. Conversely, holding the framework fixed and increasing the adsorbate's largest heavy-atom pair distance GeDi toward the bottleneck size increases the fraction of gas-phase entropy lost. This is a falsifiable proxy hypothesis transferring the reported MFI/FAU and FER/FAU confinement-rotation comparisons to this benchmark's infinite-dilution entropy-loss target; it is not an established law.
draft.rationale: Mechanism: geometric confinement restricts adsorbate rotational and configurational freedom, which the cited zeolite comparisons associate with larger entropy loss in smaller-pore frameworks. The ratio GeDi/lsd_f expresses molecule span relative to the bottleneck as a dimensionless confinement proxy. Proxy limitations: lsd_f (Zeo++ Df) is the largest sphere able to pass through a periodic free path, NOT the global cavity diameter Di that the source comparisons reference, so the mapping from 'cavity diameter' to Df is an explicit approximation; GeDi is a heavy-atom pair distance in the implicit-H representation, not a van der Waals contact span, and it is legitimately zero for 54 single-site training cases (ratio then 0, not excluded); lsd_f has no zeros in training (min 0.85684 A) so the ratio is finite across training support. The ratio is dimensionless by construction, so no q-normalization is needed and no q-ratio=1 physical-threshold claim is made. AV is deliberately not used because it is a mass-specific fixed-probe accessibility, not molecule-specific free volume.
draft.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if, within the training regime (lsd_f in [0.85684, 7.68726] A, GeDi in [0, 10.97181443] A), entropy_loss_over_R does not decrease with increasing lsd_f at fixed GeDi, or if the apparent relation disappears when ASA/AV (probe-accessible area/volume) are held fixed — indicating the signal is explained by overall framework accessibility rather than bottleneck confinement. A competing explanation is that Df correlates with framework density or connectivity rather than rotational confinement; if loss trends follow density but not GeDi/lsd_f within Df strata, the bottleneck mechanism is not supported. Additionally, if adsorbates with GeDi exceeding lsd_f (geometrically unable to pass) do not show distinctly higher loss, the confinement interpretation fails.
draft.proxy_assumptions: Assumes (1) the bottleneck free-sphere diameter Df is an adequate stand-in for the cavity-diameter confinement measure used in the reported FER/FAU comparison, even though Df, Dif, and global Di are distinct quantities; (2) the largest heavy-atom pair distance GeDi proxies the molecular rotational envelope, ignoring hydrogens and side-group orientations; (3) infinite-dilution, rigid-framework conditions comparable to the target; (4) rotational confinement dominates the entropy-loss variation attributable to this descriptor, with translational contributions left to other descriptors. These are proxy assumptions motivated by conditional source evidence (E01, E02, E04, E06), not established causality; source-specific percentages (e.g., 38% vs 20%) are not used as constants.
draft.boundary_behavior: Finite across training support: lsd_f in [0.85684, 7.68726] A has no zero values, so GeDi/lsd_f is always defined; GeDi is legitimately zero for 54 single-site cases (descriptor value 0, physically interpreted as a point-like rotor with maximal rotational freedom relative to any bottleneck, not an error). As lsd_f grows at fixed GeDi the ratio tends to 0 smoothly; large ratios arise when GeDi exceeds the bottleneck, flagging molecules geometrically hindered from passing through the periodic path.

This is a falsifiable proxy hypothesis transferring the reported MFI/FAU and FER/FAU confinement-rotation comparisons to this benchmark's infinite-dilution entropy-loss target; it is not an established law.
draft_candidate.rationale: Mechanism: geometric confinement restricts adsorbate rotational and configurational freedom, which the cited zeolite comparisons associate with larger entropy loss in smaller-pore frameworks. The ratio GeDi/lsd_f expresses molecule span relative to the bottleneck as a dimensionless confinement proxy. Proxy limitations: lsd_f (Zeo++ Df) is the largest sphere able to pass through a periodic free path, NOT the global cavity diameter Di that the source comparisons reference, so the mapping from 'cavity diameter' to Df is an explicit approximation; GeDi is a heavy-atom pair distance in the implicit-H representation, not a van der Waals contact span, and it is legitimately zero for 54 single-site training cases (ratio then 0, not excluded); lsd_f has no zeros in training (min 0.85684 A) so the ratio is finite across training support. The ratio is dimensionless by construction, so no q-normalization is needed and no q-ratio=1 physical-threshold claim is made. AV is deliberately not used because it is a mass-specific fixed-probe accessibility, not molecule-specific free volume.
draft_candidate.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if, within the training regime (lsd_f in [0.85684, 7.68726] A, GeDi in [0, 10.97181443] A), entropy_loss_over_R does not decrease with increasing lsd_f at fixed GeDi, or if the apparent relation disappears when ASA/AV (probe-accessible area/volume) are held fixed — indicating the signal is explained by overall framework accessibility rather than bottleneck confinement. A competing explanation is that Df correlates with framework density or connectivity rather than rotational confinement; if loss trends follow density but not GeDi/lsd_f within Df strata, the bottleneck mechanism is not supported. Additionally, if adsorbates with GeDi exceeding lsd_f (geometrically unable to pass) do not show distinctly higher loss, the confinement interpretation fails.
draft_candidate.proxy_assumptions: Assumes (1) the bottleneck free-sphere diameter Df is an adequate stand-in for the cavity-diameter confinement measure used in the reported FER/FAU comparison, even though Df, Dif, and global Di are distinct quantities; (2) the largest heavy-atom pair distance GeDi proxies the molecular rotational envelope, ignoring hydrogens and side-group orientations; (3) infinite-dilution, rigid-framework conditions comparable to the target; (4) rotational confinement dominates the entropy-loss variation attributable to this descriptor, with translational contributions left to other descriptors. These are proxy assumptions motivated by conditional source evidence (E01, E02, E04, E06), not established causality; source-specific percentages (e.g., 38% vs 20%) are not used as constants.
draft_candidate.boundary_behavior: Finite across training support: lsd_f in [0.85684, 7.68726] A has no zero values, so GeDi/lsd_f is always defined; GeDi is legitimately zero for 54 single-site cases (descriptor value 0, physically interpreted as a point-like rotor with maximal rotational freedom relative to any bottleneck, not an error). As lsd_f grows at fixed GeDi the ratio tends to 0 smoothly; large ratios arise when GeDi exceeds the bottleneck, flagging molecules geometrically hindered from passing through the periodic path.

review_issues.explanation: The source comparisons motivating this draft (E02: 'the average cavity diameter is a descriptor ... indicates the extent of confinement'; E04: MFI vs FAU) reference a global/average cavity diameter Di. The formula instead uses lsd_f, which is Zeo++ Df: the largest sphere able to pass through a periodic free path — a bottleneck quantity, explicitly NOT global cavity Di. The mapping Df -> cavity-diameter confinement is an unverified proxy substitution; frameworks with identical Df can have very different cavity sizes, so the direction claim at fixed GeDi may not track the reported cavity-diameter effect.

GeDi is the largest heavy-atom pair distance in the original implicit-H/heavy-atom representation, not a van der Waals contact span or rotational envelope. The hypothesis interprets it as proxying the 'molecular rotational envelope', but hydrogen positions and side-group orientations — which directly affect rotational freedom — are excluded. The mapping is plausible but unverified; no source evidence establishes GeDi as a rotational-freedom measure.

GeDi is legitimately zero for 54 single-site training cases, giving descriptor value 0. The draft's boundary interpretation ('point-like rotor with maximal rotational freedom relative to any bottleneck') is an added physical claim: single-atom and linear adsorbates also lose rotational entropy differently (rotor_domains constraint requires explicit rotor_case treatment of native single-site/linear/nonlinear inertia), and the ratio GeDi/lsd_f silently collapses all rotor classes onto one scale without the explicit rotor_case branch the formula rules anticipate for native inertia-related quantities. The derivative check confirms the descriptor is flat on these 54 cases (nonzero_fraction 0.9771 ≈ 1 - 54/2361), so the confinement mechanism is untestable there.

The falsification criterion treats 'adsorbates with GeDi exceeding lsd_f' as 'geometrically unable to pass'. This over-reads Df: lsd_f is the largest sphere passing along a periodic free path, not an adsorption-feasibility threshold. Molecules wider than Df can still reside in larger cavities; adsorption at infinite dilution does not require traversal of the bottleneck in the same sense. This threshold-like reading also conflicts with the stated rule that proxy ratios do not carry physical equality/threshold meaning.

Source evidence is conditional and narrow: E01/E04 are MFI-vs-FAU comparisons for linear alkanes; E02 is FER-vs-FAU; E06 concerns MCM-22 supercages at 450-850 K diffusion context with only a qualitative radius-of-gyration argument, and its mechanism card is 'SOURCE_PROPOSES_POSSIBLE_EFFECT'. Transfer to the benchmark's infinite-dilution, pure-silica, all-framework setting is a hypothesis; temperature, loading, and framework chemistry are unresolved in the excerpts. Source-specific percentages (38% vs 20%, 3-fold) are correctly not used as constants, but no source directly supports a GeDi/lsd_f ratio functional form — the ratio is a new, unvalidated combination.

The mechanism family is labeled 'rotation', but the ratio GeDi/lsd_f conflates translational/configurational confinement (span vs bottleneck) with rotational freedom. E03 and E07 indicate entropy loss has both translational and rotational contributions with distinguishable partition-function roles; attributing the whole ratio signal to rotation is an unverified mechanism assignment. The draft acknowledges translational contributions elsewhere, but the mechanism_family tag does not reflect this ambiguity.

The knowledge graph provides no edge linking the target (entropy_loss_over_R) to GeDi or lsd_f, and no edge between lsd_f and framework density/connectivity. Absent edges are unknown, not disproof; the competing explanation raised in the falsification criteria (Df correlating with density or connectivity rather than confinement) cannot be confirmed or excluded from the provided graph.

The draft's physical_prediction states loss_direction 'decreasing' with lsd_f while the field conditional_proxy_target_direction is 'increasing'; the intended monotonic direction of the target under the conditional is stated in prose but the structured fields are not mutually consistent, and no target values are provided to resolve which convention applies. Recorded as an ambiguity; not resolved by editing the draft.

final_candidate.hypothesis: Conditional on the same framework (lsd_f, lsd_p, AV, ASA, density held fixed) and the same adsorbate mass and second moment, adsorbates with a larger mass-normalized largest principal moment (maximum(PMI2,PMI3)/MW, proportional to a mean-squared heavy-atom radius of gyration about the principal axis) are geometrically more extended and therefore have more gas-phase rotational/configurational freedom that can be suppressed inside the pore. Transferring the reported MFI/FAU comparison, in which tighter confinement coincided with a larger fraction of gas-phase entropy lost (E01, E04, C1, C4), and the reported statement that adsorption entropic losses involve both translational and rotational motions (E03, C3), entropy_loss_over_R is hypothesized to increase with this descriptor. This is a falsifiable proxy hypothesis, not an established law.
final_candidate.rationale: The descriptor rescales the largest heavy-atom principal moment by molecular weight, giving a proxy for molecular extension (gyration-like radius) rather than absolute inertia, so it partially separates 'extended molecule' from 'heavy molecule'. Limitations: PMI values come from the implicit-H/heavy-atom representation and ignore hydrogen mass distribution, so they are not true all-atom inertias; PMI/MW is proportional to a mean-squared radius only under uniform-mass interpretation; AV remains a mass-specific fixed-probe accessibility and is not used here as molecular free volume; no claim is made that lsd_p equals a cavity diameter. The mechanism (rotational/configurational freedom suppressed by confinement) is a conditional transfer from zeolite comparisons, not demonstrated causality in this benchmark.
final_candidate.falsification_criteria: If, holding the framework descriptors fixed, entropy_loss_over_R decreases or is uncorrelated with maximum(PMI2,PMI3)/MW across the training set, the proxy hypothesis is falsified. Competing explanations that would nullify novelty or mechanism: (1) the descriptor is collinear with simpler size proxies already used (Vol, GeDi) and adds no independent information; (2) the apparent effect is driven by MW alone rather than the inertia-per-mass ratio; (3) heavy-atom PMIs misrepresent rotational inertia for hydrogen-rich adsorbates so strongly that the sign of the conditional effect is an artifact.
final_candidate.proxy_assumptions: Assumes maximum(PMI2,PMI3)/MW is a monotone proxy for molecular extension controlling how much rotational/configurational freedom is lost on confinement. Rotor_case handling is explicit: for nonlinear adsorbates the maximum selects PMI3; for linear adsorbates PMI1 is a legitimate zero and PMI2=PMI3 so the maximum selects the transverse moment; for single-site adsorbates all PMIs are legitimately zero and the descriptor evaluates to 0, encoding the branch assumption of negligible rotational entropy loss. All q-values use fixed positive training references (PMI2_ref=93.27992783, PMI3_ref=125.4948325, MW_ref=74.07316494); q-ratio=1 is not a physical equality threshold. Native zeros are preserved; no median imputation is applied.
final_candidate.boundary_behavior: Finite training support; descriptor is non-negative and finite on the training domain (PMI2 in [0, 2299.281763], PMI3 in [0, 2414.631462], MW in [16.03130013, 184.1463299] with MW_ref = 74.07316494 > 0, so q_MW > 0 everywhere and no division by zero). Legitimate native zeros are preserved: single-site adsorbates have all PMIs legitimately zero, giving descriptor exactly 0; for linear adsorbates PMI1 is a legitimate zero but never enters the expression because the maximum is taken over PMI2 and PMI3, where PMI2 = PMI3 selects the transverse moment; for nonlinear adsorbates the maximum selects PMI3 (PMI3 >= PMI2 >= PMI1 by construction of principal moments). No median imputation of physical zeros is applied.

In the following appendix , we derive the entropy of adsorption in the case of infinite dilution and show how it may be related to familiar thermodynamic quantities ( cf . eq 5 ) . To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as $$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$ where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. descriptor_candidate.hypothesis: Conditional on the same framework (lsd_f, lsd_p, AV, ASA, density held fixed) and the same adsorbate mass and second moment, adsorbates with a larger mass-normalized largest principal moment (maximum(PMI2,PMI3)/MW, proportional to a mean-squared heavy-atom radius of gyration about the principal axis) are geometrically more extended and therefore have more gas-phase rotational/configurational freedom that can be suppressed inside the pore. Transferring the reported MFI/FAU comparison, in which tighter confinement coincided with a larger fraction of gas-phase entropy lost (E01, E04, C1, C4), and the reported statement that adsorption entropic losses involve both translational and rotational motions (E03, C3), entropy_loss_over_R is hypothesized to increase with this descriptor. This is a falsifiable proxy hypothesis, not an established law.
descriptor_candidate.rationale: The descriptor rescales the largest heavy-atom principal moment by molecular weight, giving a proxy for molecular extension (gyration-like radius) rather than absolute inertia, so it partially separates 'extended molecule' from 'heavy molecule'. Limitations: PMI values come from the implicit-H/heavy-atom representation and ignore hydrogen mass distribution, so they are not true all-atom inertias; PMI/MW is proportional to a mean-squared radius only under uniform-mass interpretation; AV remains a mass-specific fixed-probe accessibility and is not used here as molecular free volume; no claim is made that lsd_p equals a cavity diameter. The mechanism (rotational/configurational freedom suppressed by confinement) is a conditional transfer from zeolite comparisons, not demonstrated causality in this benchmark.
descriptor_candidate.falsification_criteria: If, holding the framework descriptors fixed, entropy_loss_over_R decreases or is uncorrelated with maximum(PMI2,PMI3)/MW across the training set, the proxy hypothesis is falsified. Competing explanations that would nullify novelty or mechanism: (1) the descriptor is collinear with simpler size proxies already used (Vol, GeDi) and adds no independent information; (2) the apparent effect is driven by MW alone rather than the inertia-per-mass ratio; (3) heavy-atom PMIs misrepresent rotational inertia for hydrogen-rich adsorbates so strongly that the sign of the conditional effect is an artifact.
descriptor_candidate.proxy_assumptions: Assumes maximum(PMI2,PMI3)/MW is a monotone proxy for molecular extension controlling how much rotational/configurational freedom is lost on confinement. To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. In the following appendix , we derive the entropy of adsorption in the case of infinite dilution and show how it may be related to familiar thermodynamic quantities ( cf . eq 5 ) . To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as $$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$ where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. The conditional prediction (vary PMI3, hold PMI2/MW fixed, loss increasing) does not hold across the stated full training regime [0, max] for PMI3. Wherever q_PMI2 > q_PMI3 (see definition issue), the descriptor equals q_PMI2/q_MW and is INSENSITIVE to PMI3, so the descriptor is piecewise-constant rather than monotonically increasing in PMI3. The expression_check claim of descriptor_direction 'increasing' with regime_input PMI3 over quantiles [0.0, 1.0] is therefore not guaranteed on the training domain.

Narrative/formula mismatch and non-homogeneous combination: the hypothesis and rationale describe the native quantity maximum(PMI2,PMI3)/MW (units angstrom^2*amu/g/mol), but the formula operates on q-normalized values whose ratio to q_MW is a different, dimensionless number depending on three unrelated reference constants. maximum(q_PMI2, q_PMI3)/q_MW is dimensionless but physically non-homogeneous (max over two quantities with different scale factors); it is not proportional to the native mass-normalized largest moment with a single constant of proportionality, so the gyration-proxy interpretation only approximately carries over.

Mixed-representation mass normalization: PMI2/PMI3 are heavy-atom/implicit-H proxies while MW is the adsorbate molecular weight (including hydrogen mass). The draft itself acknowledges PMI/MW is proportional to a mean-squared radius of gyration 'only under uniform-mass interpretation'; whether the heavy-atom PMIs use atomic masses or unit masses per heavy atom is unresolved in the input definitions, so the mass-normalization mixing (H mass in denominator, possibly absent in numerator) is an unquantified inconsistency.

None of the cited items directly reports that more EXTENDED adsorbates (larger mass-normalized moment) lose a larger entropy fraction at FIXED framework; that adsorbate-side direction is an extrapolated transfer of the confinement comparison. The limit test (MW -> positive_infinity, expected descriptor value 0) holds PMI2/PMI3 fixed while mass diverges, which is unphysical: inertia grows with molecular mass and size, so this limit corresponds to no real molecular regime. appended.name: bottleneck_pair_span_ratio
appended.hypothesis: Conditional on the same adsorbate (GeDi held fixed), frameworks with a larger largest free passing sphere (lsd_f) allow more retained rotational and configurational freedom, so the reported pattern that stronger geometric confinement coincides with larger entropy loss on adsorption implies entropy_loss_over_R decreases as lsd_f increases. Conversely, holding the framework fixed and increasing the adsorbate's largest heavy-atom pair distance GeDi toward the bottleneck size increases the fraction of gas-phase entropy lost. This is a falsifiable proxy hypothesis transferring the reported MFI/FAU and FER/FAU confinement-rotation comparisons to this benchmark's infinite-dilution entropy-loss target; it is not an established law.
appended.rationale: Mechanism: geometric confinement restricts adsorbate rotational and configurational freedom, which the cited zeolite comparisons associate with larger entropy loss in smaller-pore frameworks. The ratio GeDi/lsd_f expresses molecule span relative to the bottleneck as a dimensionless confinement proxy. Proxy limitations: lsd_f (Zeo++ Df) is the largest sphere able to pass through a periodic free path, NOT the global cavity diameter Di that the source comparisons reference, so the mapping from 'cavity diameter' to Df is an explicit approximation; GeDi is a heavy-atom pair distance in the implicit-H representation, not a van der Waals contact span, and it is legitimately zero for 54 single-site training cases (ratio then 0, not excluded); lsd_f has no zeros in training (min 0.85684 A) so the ratio is finite across training support. The ratio is dimensionless by construction, so no q-normalization is needed and no q-ratio=1 physical-threshold claim is made. AV is deliberately not used because it is a mass-specific fixed-probe accessibility, not molecule-specific free volume.
appended.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if, within the training regime (lsd_f in [0.85684, 7.68726] A, GeDi in [0, 10.97181443] A), entropy_loss_over_R does not decrease with increasing lsd_f at fixed GeDi, or if the apparent relation disappears when ASA/AV (probe-accessible area/volume) are held fixed — indicating the signal is explained by overall framework accessibility rather than bottleneck confinement. A competing explanation is that Df correlates with framework density or connectivity rather than rotational confinement; if loss trends follow density but not GeDi/lsd_f within Df strata, the bottleneck mechanism is not supported. Additionally, if adsorbates with GeDi exceeding lsd_f (geometrically unable to pass) do not show distinctly higher loss, the confinement interpretation fails.
appended.proxy_assumptions: Assumes (1) the bottleneck free-sphere diameter Df is an adequate stand-in for the cavity-diameter confinement measure used in the reported FER/FAU comparison, even though Df, Dif, and global Di are distinct quantities; (2) the largest heavy-atom pair distance GeDi proxies the molecular rotational envelope, ignoring hydrogens and side-group orientations; (3) infinite-dilution, rigid-framework conditions comparable to the target; (4) rotational confinement dominates the entropy-loss variation attributable to this descriptor, with translational contributions left to other descriptors. These are proxy assumptions motivated by conditional source evidence (E01, E02, E04, E06), not established causality; source-specific percentages (e.g., 38% vs 20%) are not used as constants.
appended.boundary_behavior: Finite across training support: lsd_f in [0.85684, 7.68726] A has no zero values, so GeDi/lsd_f is always defined; GeDi is legitimately zero for 54 single-site cases (descriptor value 0, physically interpreted as a point-like rotor with maximal rotational freedom relative to any bottleneck, not an error). As lsd_f grows at fixed GeDi the ratio tends to 0 smoothly; large ratios arise when GeDi exceeds the bottleneck, flagging molecules geometrically hindered from passing through the periodic path.
